items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S706

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the tax law, in relation to rules and regulations
necessary for the implementation of video lottery gaming


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This legislation is intended to clarify the types of video lottery
games that are permitted at video lottery facilities in the State.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 on the bill amends Subdivisions b and c of Section 1617-a of
the tax law, as amended by Section 2 of Part Z3 of Chapter 62 of the
laws of 2003. Subdivision b sets forth revised time periods for which
video gaming machines can be operating at vendor tracks having fewer
than 1,575 video lottery machines and vendor tracks having more than
1,575 video lottery machines. Subdivision c is amended to state that
rules and regulations promulgated for the implementation of video
lottery gaming must provide for lottery versions of any game capable
of generating random results, including but not limited to roulette,
baccarat, and "21", as approved by the division.

Section 2 of this bill is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This legislation recognizes that in addition to the electronic
versions of games currently offered, the State's video lottery program
can offer other games that are based on the same game features that
have been traditionally included in the State Lottery's online games
and allows for such other games to be offered at vendor tracks in New
York State.  Surrounding States already allow other games of chance
and New Yorkers and visitors are spending their funds in those States.
Enactment of this bill will allow video lottery facilities to compete
successfully with racinos and other gaming facilities in neighboring
states.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Undetermined increase in revenue to State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect in 30 days; provided that the amendments
made to Section 1617-a of the tax law by section one of this act shall
not affect the repeal of such section and shall expire and be deemed
repealed therewith.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S706A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the tax law, in relation to rules and regulations
necessary for the implementation of video lottery gaming


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This legislation is intended to clarify the types of video lottery
games that are permitted at video lottery facilities in the State.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill amends Subdivisions band c of Section 1617-a of
the tax law, as amended by Section 2 of Part Z3 of Chapter 62 of the
laws of 2003. Subdivision b sets forth revised time periods for which
video gaming machines can operate at vendor tracks having fewer than
1,575 video lottery machines and vendor tracks having more than 1,575
video lottery machines. Subdivision c is amended to state that rules
and regulations promulgated for the implementation of video lottery
gaming must provide for lottery versions of any game capable of
generating random results, including but not limited to roulette,
baccarat, and "21 ", as approved by the division. Subdivision d is
created to protect the state's revenues by establishing a labor peace
agreement between labor organizations and video lottery facilities.
Labor organizations are prevented from engaging in work stoppages,
picketing, boycotts, and any other economic interference while
obtaining the right to unionize employees for new positions created in
relation to electronic table games at existing video lottery
facilities, with the exception of Buffalo Raceway/Fairgrounds in Erie
County. The labor peace agreement shall apply universally to any video
lottery facilities opening a after the effective date of the bill.

Section 2 of this bill is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation recognizes that in addition to the electronic
versions of games currently offered, the State's video lottery program
can offer other games that are based on the same game features that
have been traditionally included in the State Lottery's online games
and allows for such other games to be offered at vendor tracks in New
York State. Surrounding states already allow other games of chance and
New Yorkers and visitors are spending their funds in those states.
Enactment of this bill will allow video lottery facilities to compete
successfully with racinos and other gaming facilities in neighboring
states. The labor peace agreement will ensured continued positive
labor relations between video lottery facilities and their employees.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Undetermined increase in revenue to State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect in 30 days; provided that the amendments
made to Section 1617-a of the tax law by section one of this act shall
not affect the repeal of such section and shall expire and be deemed
repealed therewith.

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This legislation is intended to clarify the types of video lottery

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

- Subdivision b sets forth revised time periods for which video gaming
machines can operate at vendor tracks having fewer than 1,575 video

- Subdivision c is amended to state that rules and regulations

as approved by the division.

- Subdivision d is created to protect the state's revenues by
establishing a labor peace agreement between labor organizations and
video lottery facilities. Labor organizations are prevented from
engaging in work stoppages, picketing, boycotts, and any other
economic interference while obtaining the right to unionize employees
for new positions created in relation to electronic table games at
existing video lottery facilities, with the exception of Buffalo
Raceway/Fairgrounds in Erie County. The labor peace agreement shall
apply universally to any video lottery facilities opening a after the
effective date of the bill. Section 2 of this bill is the effective
date.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation recognizes that in addition to the electronic
versions of games currently offered, the State's video lottery program
can offer other games that are based on the same game features that
have been traditionally included in the State Lottery's online games
and allows for such other games to be offered at vendor tracks in New
York State.

Surrounding states already allow other games of chance and New Yorkers
and visitors are spending their funds in those states. Enactment of
this bill will allow video lottery facilities to compete successfully
with racinos and other gaming facilities in neighboring states. The
labor peace agreement will ensured continued positive labor relations
between video lottery facilities and their employees.

This amendment to a "D" print was for technical reasons related
changing the effective date from 2009 to 2010. That is the only change
to this bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill should raise at least $ 100 Million to support State
Education Programs.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect in 30 days; provided that the amendments
made to Section 1617-a of the tax law by section one of this act shall
not affect the repeal of such section and shall expire and be deemed
repealed therewith.

summary: Relates to regulations implementing video lottery gaming in this state; sets minimum and maximum hours of operation based upon the number of terminals offered by vendor tracks; requires regulations for games capable of generating random results.
